name: KITTI Depth Prediction Benchmark
ability_definition: The ability to judge which of several objects is closer or farther away from you, or to judge the distance between you and an object.

task_realism.reasoning: Estimating distances to cars, pedestrians, and road structure from real street imagery closely mirrors a core workplace use of depth perception: driving and vehicle operation. It covers none of the close-range work depth perception supports, such as operating cranes or forklifts, manipulating tools, or catching objects. Workers also judge distance to act, not to produce an exhaustive per-pixel map.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: It uses real sensor data, measured LiDAR ground truth, and a hidden test server, which keeps results honest. Conditions are otherwise idealized. Inputs are static single frames from one calibrated camera, with no motion parallax, binocular cues, or active viewpoint change. There is no time pressure, no consequence of error, and only a narrow input distribution: daytime, fair weather, German roads, one sensor rig.

construct_coverage.reasoning: SILog captures relative ordering, and absRel and RMSE capture absolute metric distance, so both halves of the O*NET definition are measured. Coverage is still limited. Scenes are only driving environments, depth is capped at about 80 m, and LiDAR ground truth is sparse and misses thin or reflective objects. It tests only monocular perception, with no near-field or indoor depth and no explicit judgment of the distance between two objects.

format_match.reasoning: The input is a genuine work artifact, a real camera image of a real scene. The output is a dense depth map, a machine-oriented representation rather than the discrete judgments or distance-guided actions a worker produces, such as 'that car is about 30 m ahead' or braking in time. Aggregate pixel error metrics do not weight the safety-relevant objects that matter in practice.

transferability_reasoning: KITTI measures egocentric metric and relative depth on real driving imagery against measured ground truth, a reasonably direct probe of the distance-judgment component of Depth Perception. Transfer is limited by the narrow scene domain, static monocular single-frame conditions without time pressure or binocular and motion cues, and a per-pixel output format unlike the action-oriented judgments workers make. It is moderately predictive of driving-style distance estimation but weakly predictive of depth perception across the broader range of workplace tasks.

2020.metric: SILog (scale-invariant logarithmic error ×100, on the official KITTI test server; lower is better)
2020.human_reference: General adult workforce who rely on depth perception at work (e.g., drivers, equipment operators), judging distances to objects in outdoor road scenes
